If you miss the golden era of arcade brawlers but want something that looks and feels like it belongs in the modern day, The TakeOver is a total no-brainer.

For me, the absolute highlight of this game is the spectacular soundtrack. It is an absolute masterpiece. The graphics are equally beautiful. Instead of going for the overused, low-res pixel art route, the developers crafted gorgeous, highly detailed 3D models with crisp animations and vibrant, stylized backgrounds. It gives the classic side-scrolling action a completely fresh and premium look.
The combat is fluid, the combo system is satisfying (especially characters like Jackson and Megan with their range and speed), and the mechanical response is top-tier.

The only real downside is that the game is very short. You can blast through the main story mode in just a hour or less.
That being said, at its price point—especially when picked up on a sale—it offers incredible value.
Highly recommended!

At current discounts, go for it. My reservation over the years seems founded, in that it's a pixel era game done with full graphics and those can often feel like using paper cutouts.

This does have that feeling. But decent work has gone in to shifting the perspective in the maps from the strict 2D mode - but not in too fancy a way as to be obstructive.

The visuals are garish, but nicely designed - doing the tall sprite cabinet game approach nicely, with all the usual stuff we know and expect from this genre.

Addition of a gun is novel, not played enough to see this really come into its own.

I'm sure as I play more I'll get more used to precisely where I am standing and where the enemy pickups are. At the moment it's like, ok that didn't pick up, try again lower down the screen.

Also the finishers at the end of combos are gonna take some getting used to. Great when I pull them off, but too often I'm not quite sure if I'm at the end of a combo and end up going up or down the screen rather than those directions being used as part of my chosen finisher.

I was playing on hard, but I don't think any of that is down to things which would be affected by that - which I expect is just how aggressive the enemies are and how much health they have... and perhaps how much there is around to pick up.

The music is good, I also appreciate enemies with battle jackets and heroines in Latex catsuits.

But if you're looking for a really fluid retro brawler, this isn't it. You'd be better going for a less fruity take than this. So far this seems to be for people like me who have played a ton of these over the years and appreciate the references and the new riffs on the old formula.

If you're looking for a modern beat 'em up that respects (and even imitates) the classics like Streets of Rage and Final Fight, The Takeover is worthy. Gorgeous 3d graphics with reflections and lens flares (too much lens flares). Big characters that are almost half the screen. The bar looks particularly detailed and great. For controls, not as refined as Streets of Rage 4, the top modern beat 'em up, but still very good. Being able to shoot relatively often with a gun you never lose is nice; it's not just fisticuffs. The music is fitting and motivating. You're not forced to take health right away, it won't vanish. You can also go back left. Two little improvements that I appreciate a lot.

Coop in Remote play together works fine. I enjoyed the two arcade mini-games: driving and shooting on the highway and flying in the sky with the jet. I also liked the special level where you can just shoot (no punching or kicking), but I wish there had been more than one type of enemy with more animations. No leaderboards even though a bare-minimum and only local high score list is there. Not getting extra lives for scores was missed and made picking up those vanishing collectibles even more useless. Be aware that the difficulty is reset to normal when you restart the game. A playthrough will last you around 2 hours and a half.

The TakeOver, developed and published by Pelikan13, is a side-scrolling beat ’em up that firmly roots itself in the traditions of arcade-era brawlers while layering in just enough modern design to feel relevant. It’s a game that knows exactly what it wants to be—a straightforward, action-heavy experience built around tight combat, stylized presentation, and cooperative play. Rather than attempting to reinvent the genre, it focuses on refining the familiar formula, delivering a polished tribute that captures the spirit of classics without straying too far from their blueprint.

At the center of the experience is its combat system, which balances accessibility with a satisfying level of depth. Basic attacks, grabs, and special moves form the foundation, but the inclusion of a combo system adds a layer of engagement that encourages players to stay aggressive and maintain momentum. Successfully chaining attacks builds up energy that can be spent on powerful abilities, creating a rhythm where positioning, timing, and crowd control become increasingly important. While the controls are easy to learn, mastering the flow of combat—especially on higher difficulties—requires a more deliberate approach, rewarding players who take the time to understand enemy patterns and spacing.

Progression unfolds across a series of linear stages filled with waves of enemies, environmental hazards, and occasional set-piece moments that break up the pacing. These sequences, such as vehicle chases or other scripted diversions, inject variety into the gameplay and prevent it from becoming too repetitive. Even so, the core loop remains consistent throughout, and while it is undeniably fun, extended sessions can start to reveal its limitations. Enemy types, though varied in appearance, often behave in predictable ways, which can make encounters feel routine after a while.

The game’s roster of playable characters adds some welcome diversity to the experience. Each fighter has their own attributes and subtle differences in playstyle, encouraging experimentation and offering replay value for those who want to explore different approaches. This is further supported by additional modes beyond the standard campaign, including survival-style challenges and variations that alter how characters are used within a run. These features help extend the game’s lifespan, though they don’t drastically change the core experience.

Visually, The TakeOver strikes a balance between retro inspiration and modern presentation. Character sprites are detailed and expressive, while environments blend 2D artwork with layered effects that give the stages a sense of depth. The comic book-style cutscenes reinforce the game’s tone, delivering its crime-driven narrative with a stylized flair that fits the genre. The story itself is simple and functional, serving mainly as a backdrop for the action rather than a focal point, but it succeeds in maintaining a consistent, cinematic feel throughout.

One of the game’s standout elements is its audio design, particularly the soundtrack. The music carries a strong, energetic presence that complements the on-screen action, drawing clear influence from classic beat ’em up scores while incorporating a modern edge. It enhances the pacing of fights and helps sustain the game’s momentum, especially during more intense encounters. Combined with responsive sound effects, it contributes significantly to the overall sense of impact during combat.

Despite its strengths, the game does have its shortcomings. Its commitment to classic design means it rarely steps outside established conventions, which can make it feel derivative at times. The lack of online multiplayer is also a notable omission, especially given how central cooperative play is to the genre’s appeal. Additionally, while the combat system is solid, it doesn’t evolve significantly over time, leading to a degree of repetition that may limit long-term engagement for some players.

Even with these limitations, The TakeOver succeeds in delivering a focused and enjoyable experience. It understands the fundamentals of what makes a beat ’em up satisfying and executes them with confidence, offering a game that is easy to pick up yet capable of providing a challenge when pushed. It may not redefine the genre, but it doesn’t need to—its strength lies in how well it embraces its influences and delivers on them.

In the end, The TakeOver stands as a well-crafted homage to classic arcade brawlers, offering a polished, action-packed experience that will resonate most with fans of the genre. It prioritizes fun, responsiveness, and style over innovation, resulting in a game that feels both nostalgic and accessible, even if it occasionally leans too heavily on familiarity.

Para aquellos que disfrutan los Beat,em ups ,the takeover toma la inspiración de juegos como Final Fight o Streets of Rage, pero con un toque de generación actual, además de introducir algunas ideas nuevas.

La historia es muy sencilla la ciudad de Steel Haven ha sido tomada por la unión de diferentes bandas criminales, estos secuestran la hija adoptiva del policía Ethan y su mujer Megan. Estos se unen en su búsqueda con la ayuda de su cuñado Connor. Toda la historia está narrada a través de un estilo comic, ilustrada pobremente con un estilo visual completamente diferente al del juego principal, pero que añaden un poco de contexto al recorrido para las siguientes 7 etapas del viaje de los personajes.

A lo largo de los 7 capítulos el juego ofrece 2 niveles extras diferentes muy poco visto en este tipo de juegos, una persecución por las rutas de la calle arriba de un vehículo y otra persecución aérea arriba de un F-15, lo que hace que exista una variedad de entornos hostiles atractivos, además de desbloquear personajes ocultos y de emplear estrategia contra sus jefes de banda para cada nivel.
El sistema de combate te permite crear combos entre patadas, agarres y puños o combinarlos con el movimiento especial, un movimiento defensivo que elimina los enemigos que te rodean y un ataque frontal que es más potente, al realizar ambos ataques te penaliza con un poco de salud.
Los movimientos de los personajes son muy fluidos, puedes correr por todo el escenario así como rodar de arriba y abajo por la pantalla haciendo el combate más rápido y frenético, además introduce mecánicas nuevas para cada personaje, estos consiste en que llevaran un arma de fuego, que será de gran utilidad para controlar multitudes general. Otro sistema es el medido de Ira (rage) que se llenara cuando combinemos cadenas de combos, este medidor te permite ganar un periodo de aumento de poder e invulnerabilidad, otro movimiento especial también se llenara igualmente mediante cadenas de combos, este medidor te permitirá el apoyo policial que consiste en un racimo de misiles sobre el escenario para limpiar la zona, muy parecido al primer street of rage.


A nivel visual todo funciona perfecto a 60 fps, los gráficos son siempre nítidos, los niveles están renderizados en 3D y lucen excelente y realistas. A nivel audio los golpes, patadas y objetos rompiéndose se escuchan satisfactoriamente, la música es una mezcla de estilo techno con heavy metal y se siente bien acompañando la acción de la aventura.

El juego también ofrece un modo supervivencia y un modo desafío, así como un cooperativo solo local, quizás moleste un poco lo repetitivo de sus combates y la falta de juego on line, pero es un título pulido, fácil de jugar y ofrece unas buenas horas de peleas callejeras, además de su estilo estético que lo hace diferente a los demás beat em up.

*The TakeOver*
----------------------------------------------------
Um dos ultimos jogos que zerei em 2025, todo em modo co-op !. The TakeOver traz uma gameplay beat ’em up muito nostálgica e divertida, com ambientação diversificada, boas lutas contra chefes, história genérica e gráficos interessantes.

Acompanhamos um grupo de lutadores que entra em uma jornada por conta de uma criança que foi sequestrada por uma poderosa organização criminosa que domina a cidade. Então, o grupo se une para enfrentar as gangues e avançar pelos territórios controlados pela organização. A narrativa é simples, direta e esquecível; logo, todo o enredo vira uma completa bagunça, envolvendo todo tipo de gente e até mesmo monstros. Vale citar que temos 4 personagens jogáveis. Cada um possui estilo de luta, velocidade e golpes próprios, o que traz uma boa variedade ao combate, especialmente no modo co-op

Os personagens contam com animações bem trabalhadas, que dão mais peso e diversão ao combate corpo a corpo. O estilo visual utiliza cores vibrantes, relembrando os arcades clássicos sem trazer uma sensação de jogo datado. A trilha sonora mistura rock e música eletrônica, ajudando a manter a adrenalina durante os combates, e combina bem com o clima agressivo e de perigo constante presente nos cenários do game. O maior problema desse jogo é que ele acaba em um piscar de olhos: em apenas uma tarde, eu e meu primo zeramos o jogo, restando apenas os modos secundários e a busca pelo 100%. Em promoção, o game sai por menos de 10 pila, e recomendo fortemente dar uma chance caso curta o gênero.

Что ж, наверно это самый жесткий Beat 'em up который мне попадался. Сложнее даже чем проклятая версия SOR 3 (кто понял, тот понял). Пару слов об игре:
1. Игра довольно длинная, как для игры, которую надо пройти за 1 раз.
2. Враги не ждут, пока ты проведешь комбо ихним товарищам. Они зайдут тебе за спину, и проведут свое комбо. Надо постоянно дропать комбо, то бы не лишиться половину HP (да, на HARD урон лютый).
3. Добрая половина врагов умеет стрелять (в beat 'em up'е), при чем они это прекрасно делают из-за экрана, вне поля твоей видимости.
4. По классике олд скулла все боссы в конце повторяются. К тому разрабы явно вдохновились аркадными высерами Capcom, и все боссы еще с бесконечными миньонами.
А теперь самое интересное, поговорим по некоторые ачивки.
1 Пройти игру на HARD. Тут надо что-то комментировать? Пройти сложную игру на сложной сложности. И да, все в тех традициях олд скулла, никаких сохранений.
2. Пройти последнего босса без урона. Как думаете, на сколько сложный последний босс в сложной игре? Да, все плохо. Твои атаки в рандомный момент прерываются, и ты жрешь урон. Невозможно его мувсет просчитать. Ах, и да, у него в миньонах самые сильные рядовые мобы.
И вишенка на торте
3. Пройти всю игру не разу не умерев. Вот тут точно нечего комментировать. Можно только добавить бонусом, что в одном месте разрабы банально забыли положить хилку. Она должна быть, но ее нет. 95%, что твой ран закончится именно там.
Собственно сложность, это главная отличительная черта данного beat 'em up'а от других. Если кратко о других аспектах игры, то музыка и графика на высоте. По геймплею, можно закомбить сколь угодно длинное  комбо, просто тебе этого сделать не дадут) Враги разнообразные, к каждому нужен свой подход. Для самых упоротых, есть режим выживания с бесконечными волнами.
Из минусов отмечу пожалуй только отсутствие онлайна. Кооп возможен только по remote play, либо с реальным другом.

For full context, play time is around an hour and I got to the end of stage four. Big Fightn'Rage and Streets of Rage 4 fan, along with older beat'em ups. Played on Normal mode, didn't even go to the options menu until after I stopped. Double Dragon Neon and River City Girls also come to mind on what I'm used to.

I dig the music, it's pretty rocking. Sadly, I don't care for the rest of the game. The move sets are pretty basic which isn't a bad thing in of itself, The gun doesn't really do much for me because it doesn't deal more damage than a standard hit. The enemy variety is there but outside of how their attacks look I can't understand what makes them different. In the two above mentioned games, enemy variety is upfront and center to the point you really need to focus on dynamics when facing a crowd. In this, you have different models and names but almost nothing stands out except for when they feel like attacking.

On the topic of enemies attacking, I've left my back open plenty of times and I'll see foes meander around without going in to attack. Maybe it's because it was on normal mode but that felt really weird to me. Enemies are durable but they really don't do a lot about it. The Breaker guys especially will block your entire combo except the last hit and that's... kinda it. The quickest option is to just grab and knee him four times per grab. Will take you maybe three or four grabs.

I really am not the sort to rag on graphics because I grew up playing ASCII roguelikes. I'm not a shallow man. That said, the animations and graphics just look odd to me. Maybe its the frame rate they're at or that they seem stiff but something about it is off to me.

When it came to the two bosses I fought, I used the game's Rage Mode to basically erase them without really learning any movesets. The first boss had grenades blowing up all at once which blasted through my speakers, that wasn't fun. Second boss... he was there. He shot me a few times because the super mode took off around 90% of his HP except for his i-frame stances that made him immune to damage.

You can argue it's not much of a gripe but I also don't care for how, when you pause, your only option is to quit or continue. When you realize how common grenades are and how badly they'll assault you through sound, you're going to have to alt-tab out or lower your speaker volume a ton. There are many grenades. As well as grenades, items are dropping all the time but they're random baubles that increase your score or give you ammo for your sidearm. I didn't die though I came close in the fourth level, just for a burger to pop out for a full refresh. I don't know if they're randomized or come out at specific points but healing items aren't so rare.

Again, I dig some of the ideas and got to touch on the driving game mode. I dig that a lot. The rest of it... I just don't. It feels too weird. It feels very stiff for what it is and the enemies aren't really taking it seriously. It could be because I was on normal and am used to other games going hard. If you want something that is a side-scroller and really gets you going beyond just music, go with any of the above mentioned titles.

Having played a lot of beat em ups of old and modern times, I cannot say I'm convinced with "The Takeover". Impact of blows and kicks feels kind of unsatisfying, and graphics are, although 3D, not too convincing, slightly chaotic, with some aspects hard to decipher. In addition, the main characters feel kind of weird, the bully Rambo-style character a bit out of place, and some strange dimensions with the legs of the female character. When choosing the character, I had some difficulty finding one that feels okay to play. I like the soundtrack of "The Takeover", especially in the intro sequence, but once that seuqnece is over, the game didn't grab me.

Pros
1. You can do long combos which is fun.
2. The soundtrack ranges from middle of the road to great.
3. The game offers some nice unlockables such as an extra character and the ability to switch characters in game like a team.
4. The graphics reminds me of Killer Instinct which is nice and a pretty bold move when every beat em up is either pixel art or hand drawn. 
5. The campaign has some cool mini game levels that breaks from beating people up.

Cons
1. The game is way too long to complete. Unless the game has open world or rpg elements, traditional beat em ups should not take close to 2 hours to finish.
2. Enemies can be fairly tanky. So unless your doing long optimal combos they stick around and can swarm you up pretty fast which can boggle the game and pace.
3. The cutscenes are are in comic form which is a big deviation from the prerender art.
4. A lot of explosives goes off in the later stages which is really annoying. Too many hazards that interrupt flow.
5. The default controls have very awkward button map placing. Lucky you can change it.

This game is a love it, hate it kind of game. Do I still recommend it? Yes, in regards to the addicting long combos you can do, but the game has clear faults in it's pacing which makes it frustrating at times. Pick it up when it's on a good sale and you won't regret it.

Jogo maravilhoso, um mix dos melhores Beat em Up dos anos 90 com um toque de capricho!

É evidente que The Takeover busca inspiração em gigantes do gênero, como Streets of Rage e Final Fight. Ele é, sem dúvida, um beat 'em up competente, que entrega o que promete. A jogabilidade é sólida, mas, como você notou, não vai além do esperado. Ele cumpre seu papel sem inovar, o que o coloca na categoria de "bom o suficiente", mas sem o brilho de um clássico.

O ponto que realmente se destaca é a trilha sonora. Ela é legal, vibra com a ação e eleva a experiência. É o tipo de música que faz você querer continuar a briga, mesmo que o resto do jogo seja apenas "OK".

Já a parte gráfica eu achei estranha. Não é feio, mas a estética parece um pouco desalinhada, com personagens e cenários que não se encaixam perfeitamente.

Os personagens são caricatos e a história é clichê. Em um gênero onde a simplicidade do enredo é comum, a falta de carisma dos protagonistas acaba pesando. A narrativa é apenas um pano de fundo, e a ausência de algo mais cativante faz com que a experiência geral seja esquecível. The Takeover diverte, mas não tem a personalidade para marcar sua memória como os clássicos que o inspiraram.

Para quem busca o 100%....desafios como "zerar sem morrer" ou "derrotar o chefe sem levar dano" são o tipo de coisa que questiona o propósito das conquistas. Eles não agregam diversão nem uma sensação de recompensa. São apenas obstáculos artificiais que tiram o prazer de jogar.

No fim das contas, The Takeover é um jogo que vale a pena, mas só se for em uma promoção muito boa. No preço cheio, a experiência não compensa. É um jogo que diverte por um tempo, mas não é uma experiência que você vai querer revisitar.

This one is a very strange game, no doubt about it. I've seen some gameplay videos of people saying it's a great beat'em up, I wasn't going to buy it because it looked ugly to me but then I've decided to give it a chance... The game is ugly indeed. The graphics remind me of those ugly pre-rendered games from the 90's, stuff like Rise of the Robots and X-Perts for the Sega Genesis, really disgusting and cheap 3D art work. Also, the graphics from the game opening screen, the gameplay itself and the cutscenes are all different, so they knew the graphics were horrible.

The music is amazing, they even had the master Yuzo Koshiro aboard on the team, so you couldn't get it wrong. However, they still managed to mess the music programming as some sections of the game have no music and can you notice they did something wrong related to cycling the soundtracks as the game flows, LOL.

The gameplay is cool. Not the best system, but you can taste the Streets of Rage influence as you bang the bad guys all over the screen. It's kinda complex and you have a 3 different special attacks system, that goes from a classic area of effect power move that drains a bit of health, a chargeable bomb attack that hits everyone on the screen and a "rage" chargeable trigger that raises your damage drastically as gives you invincibility by auto blocking enemy attacks. You've got two basic attacks that are the punch and the kick as they play some kind of role of heavy and light attack respectively as you can alternate between them to build your combos. There is also a firearm attack move that can be reloaded as you find ammo across the stages and weapons that fall on the ground although these weapons you find weren't programmed in a very clever fashion as you lose the ability of grabbing enemies or even using regular attacks - in case of firearms such as the rifle - as you're wielding them. Pretty strange in my opinion, I've never seen any other beat'em up with those limitations regarding weapons scrounged on the fly.

If I could give it a rate, I'd give it a 4/10. It's fun, the music is cool but everything else is clearly unfinished or done in a very poor way. It seems it's the first Pelikan13 release, so maybe they will come back with more experienced developers that won't repeat mistakes committed in the past.

Quem escreve que o jogo não é fluido só pode estar louco. The TakeOver é um beat n'up extremamente satisfatório e que se apresenta como um sucessor espiritual de Streets of Rage 3... Bem, mas nós temos um Streets of Rage 4 oficial, que é superior ao The TakeOver em todos os sentidos; mesmo assim, este é um título claramente mais barato e que, mesmo assim, não fica muito atrás.

Os personagens jogáveis seguem justamente os arquétipos sustentados na série SoR (e em outras séries do estilo): um personagem com equilíbrio entre força e velocidade (claramente inspirado em Axel), um bastante forte porém lento (Max de SoR 2 é uma óbvia referência) e uma representação feminina menos forte e mais veloz (inspirada em Blaze). 

A história é tipo de filme pornô: está lá, mas você não liga para ela. O que realmente importa é descer a lenha em quem tiver pela frente, e esta parte é bastante satisfatória. Há até umas fases que fogem da lógica beat n'up; em uma você controla um veículo e sai atirando nos inimigos, e em outra você controla uma aeronave (e também sai atirando nos inimigos)... Eu realmente fiquei surpreso com essa mudança de tom.

Mas nem tudo são flores... A trilha sonora é boa, mas não é muito marcante (ela apenas está lá); há, também, um problema nos personagens inimigos, que são poucos e, por isto, não repetidos ao extremo ao longo das fases.

Bem, The TakeOver é um jogo bastante divertido e foi uma promessa que que fez justiça a quase tudo o que foi apresentado no marketing. Gosta de beat n'up? Então jogue este.
